text:
Brandon Montour is playing like Seattle's No. 1 defenseman, and the minutes say the Kraken see him that way too: 24 a night on the season and over 25 in his last ten games, including a 30-minute night in Detroit. He has 3 goals and 14 points in 18 games, a better pace than last season's 32 points in 64.

The way he plays hasn't changed since he won the Cup with Florida in 2024. He's among the fastest skaters in the league, top 4% in bursts over 20 mph, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him joining the rush far more than a typical defenseman (31% of his shots, against 17%) while setting up teammates at an 83rd-percentile rate.

The context is the catch. Seattle gets only about 48% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on at five on five, though that's five points better than when he sits. Evolving-Hockey had him near replacement level last season but noted his teammates ranked in the bottom 4% and his chance-based value was far better than his results. He's carrying a lot. We'd watch whether those heavy minutes wear on him.
